title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per preregistered rules). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution used the declared model gpt-5-mini and recorded 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not produced by the archived confirmatory summary artifacts; we reproduce the compact harmful-change mapping used by the archived scoring pipeline, provide the exact artifact locations required to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair statistic from archived per-episode traces, and treat the preregistered safety test as unresolved by the archived confirmatory summary while preserving all other preregistered inferential claims.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as aides in network operations (NetOps) for tasks ranging from intent-to-configuration translation to automated remediation. A common safety-oriented architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): a candidate configuration is checked by a deterministic verifier and, when violations are detected, verifier diagnostics are exposed to a repair model to produce corrected candidates. Prior empirical work in program repair and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) domains reports verifier-interposed repair can raise verifier-detected pass rates while exposing new failure modes and imposing interaction costs [1]–[4]. Surveys and field case studies of LLMs in NetOps/AIOps stress that read-oriented assistance does not straightforwardly imply safe closed-loop autonomous changes [5].

Motivation and research question. There is a shortage of controlled-challenge experiments that deterministically inject realistic vendor-CLI faults and measure whether verifier-guided LLM repair reduces residual unsafe or invalid configurations. A critical methodological point is intervention informativeness: verifier-guided repair can affect outcomes only when initial candidates trigger actionable diagnostics. To address this, we preregistered a deterministic controlled-fault injection (task indices 1..40), used shared controlled-fault candidates across paired arms, and fixed repair budgets in a paired confirmatory design. Our research question: does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults?
sections.related_work: Generate–verify–repair and related generate–validate–repair architectures have empirical support in code and IaC tasks where deterministic verifiers raise pass@1 or validator-pass rates and provide diagnostic signals used for repair [1], [2]. Other work demonstrates pathologies: single-verifier iterative loops can be exploited (verifier-exploitation) and verifier mediation can impose measurable interaction and compute overheads (the "verifier tax") that affect operational feasibility [3], [4]. Recent surveys and field case studies specific to agentic NetOps document positive effects for diagnostic support but caution about autonomous closed-loop changes without rigorous verification and controlled evaluation [5]. These findings motivate our preregistered controlled-challenge paired evaluation targeting vendor-CLI templates with explicit harmful-change rules and complete artifact archival for auditability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where the binary success indicator requires both a deterministic vendor-CLI verifier and simulator-based compliance agreement (joint verifier+simulator predicate). The preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest (preregistration_sha256 = 0ba66573928647f008b2cd5b9dde6708a61ae86ece55b693ace534e01e2b132c).

Execution contract and pairing semantics. Confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each preregistered task index a single deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate was produced and reused unchanged across both conditions. Exactly one sampled initial generation per pair was performed and reused by both arms; baseline denotes blind repair (no verifier diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The declared_model_version in the archived model configuration is gpt-5-mini and temperature is null/unset; null/unset is recorded but does not imply deterministic sampling.

Controlled-challenge sampling and informativeness. To ensure intervention activation we used a deterministic fault operator (deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1) that injects actionable violations (examples: dropped_required_restore, protected_interface_change, make_before_break patterns). The execution manifest records controlled_fault_assignment_sha256 = 8d0879872348ae94a45f3d674df57d6552624cd841b62ab239a280347f5275c6, source_generation_attempt_count = 40, source_valid_count = 39, source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1. The preregistered missingness rule 'complete_pair_primary' excludes a pair only if both condition executions are unscorable; this occurred once and is documented in analysis/missingness_summary.csv (see Reproducibility below).

Scoring, harmful-change mapping, and preregistered safety hypothesis. The primary success predicate required both the deterministic vendor-CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and simulator agreement. The preregistration specified a harmful-change labeling schema used to implement the preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory hypothesis: the compact operational mapping implemented by the archived scoring pipeline and used for preregistered harmful-overrepair labeling is the following deterministic rule (we reproduce it verbatim as used by the archived artifacts): any per-episode validator violation with code PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE is labeled a harmful change for the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation. Per-episode validator traces recorded violation codes in validator_trace.violation_codes and are archived for automated aggregation. The transformation artifact implementing the mapping is referenced in the execution manifests as execution/transformation_manifest.json; per-episode raw traces are in execution/raw_results.jsonl and execution/scoring/*.json.

Statistical analysis plan. The preregistered primary test is an exact paired binary test (two-sided McNemar exact or equivalent exact paired binomial), reporting absolute paired risk difference, discordant-pair counts, two-sided exact p-value, and a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile confidence interval (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Multiplicity control: a single predefined primary paired test (no multiplicity adjustment); subgroup/per-fault-class analyses are exploratory. Missingness sensitivity analyses were preregistered: (1) primary analysis excludes incomplete pairs per 'complete_pair_primary'; (2) sensitivity treats missing episodes as failures. Full raw artifacts and provider traces are archived to permit independent recomputation of any preregistered secondary aggregations.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs) with failed_episode_count = 2. Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= planned maximum 120). Source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). Run timestamps (UTC) are recorded in the execution manifest (started_at_utc = 2026-09-04T21:16:50.730326+00:00; completed_at_utc = 2026-09-04T21:19:34.370550+00:00). Stage-level instrumentation archived in deterministic_reconciliation shows valid_source_generation = 40, blind_controlled_fault_repair = 39, validator_guided_controlled_fault_repair = 39.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded (verifier-guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (both fail). The paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact) p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The archived analysis artifacts analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv contain these counts (see Reproducibility hashes below).

Missingness and exclusions. One pair was excluded under the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule because the source-generation attempt for that task was invalid/unscorable (both_missing_pairs = 1; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). The analysis/missingness_summary.csv records complete_pairs = 39 and both_missing_pairs = 1 (artifact hash provided below). No baseline-only or guarded-only single-condition infrastructure failures occurred; all exclusions and failure causes are logged in execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/raw_results.jsonl.

Preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory statistic: archived status and reproducibility path. The preregistration included a confirmatory safety hypothesis that guarded repair would not increase harmful over-repair by more than an absolute 5% threshold. The archived confirmatory analysis executor produced the primary paired binary result but did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation (secondary_results = []). The per-episode validator traces required to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair counts are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json) and contain validator_trace.violation_codes for each episode. Reproducing the preregistered harmful-overrepair paired statistic requires applying the archived harmful-change mapping (PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE -> harmful-change) to each episode's validator_trace.violation_codes and aggregating paired counts across conditions. Because the archived confirmatory summary did not include this preregistered aggregation, the preregistered harmful-overrepair test remains unresolved in the confirmatory summary we present here; the exact artifact locations and the compact deterministic mapping are provided so auditors can reproduce the preregistered aggregation without further model calls. Any counts computed outside the archived confirmatory summary are labeled exploratory in this paper.

Representative diagnostic examples. Representative per-pair JSON scoring artifacts are archived (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json, task-000002-*.json, task-000003-*.json, etc.) and illustrate typical patterns. Pair-000001 (dropped_required_restore) shows both baseline and guarded repairs reaching validity after repair; the guarded episode trace documents validator_feedback_exposed_to_model = true. Pair-000003 demonstrates a protected-interface change injected in the source; baseline repair left PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE violations after repair while guarded repair removed them and produced a valid configuration. These per-episode traces are archived for inspection and independent aggregation.

Exploratory instrumentation. The execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation provide stage-level counts and hosted-model call totals (hosted_model_call_event_count = 118) enabling exploratory computation of model-call cost per avoided failure; we present these as exploratory artifacts in the archive but label them explicitly as non-confirmatory.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and causal scope. Under the preregistered controlled-challenge and shared-candidate pairing semantics, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics substantially increased verifier+simulator-validated configuration success in the preregistered synthetic vendor-CLI task bank (approx. +20.51 percentage points). The shared initial-candidate pairing semantics isolate the causal effect of diagnostic exposure because each arm received the same controlled-fault candidate, identical repair budgets, and the same model identity and provider-call budget.

Safety and unresolved confirmatory item. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair hypothesis — a safety check that would directly quantify whether guarded repair increases harmful edits beyond the prespecified 5% threshold — was not aggregated by the archived confirmatory executor. We do not assert the preregistered safety verdict here. Instead, we (a) reproduce the compact deterministic harmful-change mapping used by the archived scoring pipeline (PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE => harmful-change), (b) document the exact archived per-episode traces and transformation artifacts required to produce the preregistered aggregation, and (c) mark the preregistered harmful-overrepair test unresolved by the archived confirmatory summary. Independent auditors can reaggregate the archived traces to compute the preregistered statistic without additional model calls.

Operational implications and verifier tax. The archived instrumentation records hosted-model calls and stage counts but our confirmatory run is not sufficient to measure large-scale operational cost/latency tradeoffs (the verifier tax). Scaling studies are required to quantify cost per avoided outage and to determine acceptable verifier budgets in production NetOps pipelines. The practical deployment decision must balance incremental correctness gains against verifier-mediated latency and financial cost.

Threats to validity. Internal validity — prompt sensitivity and sampling nondeterminism: the archived model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini and temperature = null/unset; the shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics imply exactly one sampled initial generation per pair was performed and reused, so differences arise from diagnostic exposure and subsequent repair calls. Construct validity — our primary success predicate required both deterministic verifier and simulator agreement; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain the construct validity of the success metric. External validity — single-model, single-adapter, and synthetic task-bank limit generalizability to heterogeneous production devices and workloads. Conclusion validity — n = 39 complete pairs provides useful power for the observed effect size but limits fault-class subgroup precision. All such threats are documented and linked to archived artifacts.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and operationally meaningful increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). This conclusion is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the archived deterministic verifier and simulator. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test (safety aggregation) was not computed by the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for the confirmatory claim; we publish the exact mapping and artifact locations required for independent reproduction. We release the evidence bundle for reproducible reaggregation and recommend multi-model, multi-verifier replications and larger-scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration_sha256 recorded in execution manifest). Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version recorded in execution/model_configuration.json; execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10) and cited here by immutable archive reference. Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: execution manifest records temperature = null/unset in execution/model_configuration.json; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Harmful-change mapping and reconstructability: the preregistered harmful-change rules were frozen and the archived scoring pipeline used the compact deterministic mapping reproduced in Methods (PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE => harmful-change). Per-episode raw traces and scoring artifacts required to reproduce all aggregated confirmatory and preregistered secondary statistics are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json; analysis/*.csv). Key archived artifact paths and representative hashes: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256: 7a78f9a5e735f9186833bf52c7d12643fb644bfaefade0ed1b4e5392c5a60022), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA-256: c006f8dcff29e15532f9cf95f6eb01ff1bc72c6e1aaadce5d6f6ad479d6b9cf6), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA-256: 4c9b959ba78e123d602238fa6d9a6ff0daa06c7a44f97bcfd3d6ca90343f6d9c), analysis/missingness_summary.csv (SHA-256: 05b9c4e5f8f563b76a7918bdfa4f2f0d4e3df93a00c067727acd05701154b220), execution/model_configuration.json (SHA-256 above). The study followed the preregistered stopping rule; no silent adapter substitution occurred.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and transformation manifest required to compute it are archived and available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
